text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambia press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The supreme court throws out an opposition application for president Frederick Chiluba to undergo a DNA test to establish his parentage.
- Unionised workers at the state-run Zambia Railways in the central town of Kabwe strike for improved conditions of service.
- Health minister Katele Kalumba says a just-ended polio immunisation drive was nearly derailed by a widespread rumour that the vaccine makes people sexually impotent.
- The high court throws out a libel action by vice president Godfrey Miyanda against an editor on an independent daily.
